LESSON: HOUSING THE FAMILY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: HOME SCIENCE
Strand: Home Management
Topic 2.3: Housing the Family
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Housing the Family, part of Home Management in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 HOME SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: How can the family be housed? 2. Why is room interrelationship in the house important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explain reasons for housing the family,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Housing the Family in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. categorise houses found in the community,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Housing the Family in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. describe methods of housing the family,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Housing the Family in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. relate rooms to their functions in the house,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Housing the Family in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate room interrelationship when housing the family.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Housing the Family in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. explain reasons for housing the family,

   Housing the Family helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. categorise houses found in the community,

C. describe methods of housing the family,

D. relate rooms to their functions in the house,

   Housing the Family helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. appreciate room interrelationship when housing the family.

   Housing the Family helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. deliberate on reasons for housing the family and share their views in plenary,

2. discuss, draw and model designs of different types of houses in the community using suitable locally available materials (traditional and modern). Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views on causes of accidents. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted drawing materials and model on adjustable working surfaces,

3. discuss methods of housing the family (building, buying, renting, mortgage, inheritance), factors to consider, advantages and disadvantages. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. deliberate on reasons for housing the family and share their views in plenary,
2. discuss, draw and model designs of different types of houses in the community using suitable locally available materials (traditional and modern). Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views on causes of accidents. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted drawing materials and model on adjustable working surfaces,
3. discuss methods of housing the family (building, buying, renting, mortgage, inheritance), factors to consider, advantages and disadvantages. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Housing the Family together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
25

● Creativity and Imagination: The learner shows ability to use imagination to generate new ideas as the design and prepare

models of different types of houses in the community.

● Citizenship: Learner exhibits cultural awareness as they prepare models of traditional and modern houses.

Values:
● Respect: The learner understands and appreciates diversity in cultures as they model different houses.

● Patriotism: The learner is aware of their own culture as they discuss the types of houses in their community.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Cultural awareness: Learners are made aware of their cultures as they discuss and make models of different types of houses.
